n: Al Ruwais Pleistocene sea cow fossil site
na: موقع أحفورة الأطوم البليستوسينية في الرويس
s: Last-interglacial beach deposit · fossil sea cow rib
dr: Futaisi Member, Fuwayrit Formation; about 125 ka (inferred, MIS 5e)
te: A sea cow on a 125,000-year-old beach
ta: بقرة بحر على شاطئ عمره 125 ألف عام
se: On the shore west of Al Ruwais, rocks from an ancient beach held the rib of a sea cow that grazed seagrass about 125,000 years ago
sa: على الساحل غرب الرويس حفظت صخور شاطئ قديم ضلعًا لبقرة بحر كانت ترعى الأعشاب البحرية قبل نحو 125 ألف عام
desc: A shoreline outcrop west of Al Ruwais in northern Qatar exposes the Futaisi Member of the Fuwayrit Formation, the earliest Pleistocene deposit preserved on the Qatar peninsula. The member is no more than 1 m thick and reaches about 1.5 m above present high tide: a basal lag of dolomite pebbles is overlain by cross-bedded oolitic grainstone with burrows, read as a wave-dominated foreshore to upper shoreface deposit from a Pleistocene sea-level highstand. In December 2019 a dugongid rib fragment (QM.2021.0504), about 112 mm long, was collected here; it most resembles the living dugong. Its age of about 125 ka is inferred by correlation with last-interglacial (MIS 5e) platforms, not by direct dating.
sig: A fossil sea cow from Qatar’s earliest preserved Pleistocene deposit, showing that seagrass meadows and dugong-like animals were in the Arabian Gulf by about 125,000 years ago.
refs: Pyenson, N.D., Al-Ansi, M., Fieseler, C.M., Al Jaber, K.H., Klim, K.D., LeBlanc, J., Mohamed, A.M.D., Al-Shaikh, I. & Marshall, C.D. (2022). Fossil Sirenia from the Pleistocene of Qatar: new questions about the antiquity of sea cows in the Gulf Region. PeerJ 10, e14075. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.14075
conf: Coordinates as published in the paper (N 26°06′44.6″, E 51°09′31.2″). Timeline span 130,000–115,000 years is a broad estimate for the last interglacial; the paper gives about 125 ka by correlation, not direct dating. Arabic name made for this record

n: Al Khor Towers and Ain Hleetan Well
s: Three coastal watchtowers · guarded the harbour and the town’s main well
dr: Thought to date to about 1900; Qatar Museums heritage sites HAR4161, HAR668, HAR669, HAR3552
se: Three round stone towers on the Al Khor shore once watched for ships and guarded Ain Hleetan, the well that kept the town alive
sa: ثلاثة أبراج حجرية مستديرة على ساحل الخور كانت تراقب السفن وتحرس عين حليتان، البئر التي عاشت عليها البلدة
desc: Three cylindrical stone towers stand along the coast of Al Khor in north-east Qatar, with thick stone walls and an accessible balcony. They are thought to date to about 1900 and are about 8 m tall. The towers watched ships entering Al Khor harbour and guarded the Ain Hleetan well, described by Qatar Museums as the main water source that sustained life in Al Khor. Qatar Museums lists the Eastern, Southern and Western towers and the well as separate heritage records.
sig: A compact example of how coastal Qatari towns of the pearling and fishing era defended both their harbours and their fresh water.
refs: Qatar Museums (2016). Keeping History Alive – Guide to Heritage Sites in Qatar, p. 28. https://web.archive.org/web/20170620214210/http://www.qm.org.qa/sites/default/files/user_uploads/heritage_sites_10-oct_16_small_0.pdf
Qatar Museums. Towers at Al Khor. https://qm.org.qa/en/visit/heritage-sites/al-khor-towers/
Jaidah, I. & Bourennane, M. (2010). The History of Qatari Architecture 1800–1950. Milan: Skira, p. 102. ISBN 978-8861307933
conf: Coordinates are those of the Eastern Tower (HAR4161) in the Qatar Museums heritage list (N25° 41.303 E51° 30.371); the other towers and the well lie within about 0.5 km. Construction date is approximate (about 1900). About 4 km from the existing Al Khor Island record, a different site

s: Prehistoric flint workshops on a coastal rock ridge · 41 tanged points at one spot
p: Prehistoric (described as Mesolithic by the excavator)
dr: Investigated 1959 by the Danish expedition; published 1961
te: The ridge where hunters made arrowheads
ta: التلّ الذي صنع فيه الصيادون رؤوس سهامهم
se: On a low rock ridge north of Doha, early hunters camped out of the wind and left thousands of flint chips and arrowheads
sa: على تلّ صخري منخفض شمال الدوحة احتمى صيادون قدماء من الرياح، وتركوا آلاف الشظايا ورؤوس السهام من الصوان
desc: Al Wusail is a rock ridge on Qatar’s east coast about 25 km north of Doha, running NNW–SSE about 600–700 m inland, about 1 km long and 150–200 m wide. In 1959 Danish archaeologist Viggo Nielsen found flint at 12 localities on the ridge, six of which he considered habitation sites. Locality 2, where 61 m² were examined, yielded about 5,000–6,000 flint pieces, including 41 tanged points, about 85 blades and scrapers. Nielsen found no close parallels in Qatar and placed the industry in a general Mesolithic setting.
sig: Studied by the Danish expedition in 1959, it shows early people using a sheltered coastal ridge near grazing game.
refs: Nielsen, V. (1961). Al Wusail. Mesolitiske flintpladser i Qatar [Al Wusail: Mesolithic flint sites in Qatar]. Kuml 11, 169–184. https://doi.org/10.7146/kuml.v11i11.103350
GeoNames. Al Wusayl (hill), Al Daayen, Qatar. https://www.geonames.org/search.html?q=Lusail
conf: Coordinates are the GeoNames point for Al Wusayl hill; the source gives no coordinates for the 12 localities, so their exact positions on the ridge may differ. No absolute date is published: the timeline span is a broad estimate for a pre-pottery flint industry, and Nielsen’s Mesolithic label is kept as his interpretation

s: Fort in old Doha beside Souq Waqif · police post, jail and museum
dr: Built 1880 (rebuilt 1927 by Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani); military fort 1927–1977; museum from 1978
te: The fort in the heart of old Doha
se: Beside Souq Waqif stands the Al Koot Fort, once a police post and jail, now a museum of old Qatari crafts
sa: بجوار سوق واقف تقف قلعة الكوت، التي كانت مخفرًا وسجنًا، وصارت اليوم متحفًا للحرف القطرية القديمة
desc: Al Koot Fort is a historic military fortress in the Al Bidda area of Doha, within Souq Waqif near the Corniche. Sources date it to 1880 and record that it was rebuilt in 1927 under Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani, who ruled from 1913 to 1949. It served as a police station, as a jail from 1906, and as a military fort from 1927 to 1977. Renovated in 1978, it became a museum of traditional handicrafts, fishing equipment, boats and historical photographs.
sig: A surviving fortress of old Doha whose changing uses, from jail and fort to museum, trace the city’s modern history.
conf: Coordinates from Wikipedia (25°17′12″N 51°31′51″E). Sources disagree on the construction date (1880 versus 1927); the record uses 1880 for the build and 1927 for the rebuild. About 1.3 km from the National Museum of Qatar record, a different site

s: Neolithic coastal settlement of about 6000 BC · lost and found again in 2015
el: Shagra II path about 18 m long with 4–5 dwellings
se: Near Al Wakrah, a Stone Age fishing village of stone houses was lost for decades, then found again with a second village nearby
sa: قرب الوكرة ضاعت لعقود قرية صيد من العصر الحجري ذات بيوت حجرية، ثم عُثر عليها من جديد ومعها قرية ثانية قريبة
desc: Shagra is a Neolithic site in Al Wakrah municipality, dated to about 6000 BC, first found by a French archaeological team in 1981 and described by Marie-Louise Inizan in 1988. Finds include a two-room structure, flints and the remains of fish and molluscs. After Qatar Museums Authority could not relocate it in 2010–2012, geologist Jacques LeBlanc rediscovered the site in 2015 and found Shagra II about 0.65 km to the north-west. Shagra II has a path about 18 m long with the foundations of four to five adjacent dwellings, further dwellings nearby and a possible child’s grave set in sabkha.
sig: A Neolithic settlement with house foundations in south-east Qatar, showing coastal people living on fish and shellfish about 8,000 years ago.
refs: LeBlanc, J. (2015). The Al-Shagra archeological site re-discovered (Qatar). https://www.researchgate.net/publication/299562949_The_Al-Shagra_archeological_site_re-discovered_Qatar
LeBlanc, J. (2015). The new ‘Al-Shagra II’ Site (Qatar). https://www.academia.edu/23931689/The_new_Al-Shagra_II_Site_Qatar_
conf: Coordinates are the whole-minute locality point for Shagra given by Wikipedia (24°49′N 51°22′E), not a surveyed site point; the site may lie up to about 1–2 km away. Only ‘about 6000 BC’ is published, so the end date (t1) is an estimate
